recap.summary: Week 6 was a 77.80–82.58 loss to Big Ten All Star Team — a 4.78-point defeat with three zeros in the starting nine. Lamar Jackson (Out) was started again for 0.0 while Justin Herbert sat on the bench for 8.76, which by itself was the game. Jameson Williams was started at WR2 while Detroit was on bye (0.0), and Brian Thomas posted a second straight 0.0 at WR1. Isaiah Likely (23.9) and Luther Burden (17.5) carried the scoring, and RJ Harvey (14.6) finally produced. We fall to 1-5 with the league's worst PF/PA combination. Grading the prior packet: the Herbert-over-Lamar call was correct but was not executed in the app — that is now the single most important process fix. The packet's Josh Jacobs RB1 call was wrong (he posted 0.0 again and the context has him buried at depth 4 / bench role in Green Bay) and the owner's deviation to Allgeier/Burden was the better lineup. The conditional Dameon Pierce claim was correctly left unsubmitted (Barkley's team never freed the backfield and Pierce went to ccharron33 for nothing), so waiver priority #1 is still in hand — which is exactly what saves us this week.
what_worked: Isaiah Likely at TE (23.9) — second straight elite week; he is now a legitimate sell-high consolidation chip because Oronde Gadsden backs him up
RJ Harvey at RB2 (14.6) — the ceiling-over-floor call finally paid; he stays locked in
Keeping waiver priority #1 by not submitting the conditional Pierce claim — it is the reason we can guarantee a QB this week
Cleveland DEF (10.0) — the stream-and-hold call keeps producing in a 1.0-per-sack system
what_hurt: Lamar Jackson started while Out (0.0) with Herbert's 8.76 on the bench — a 4.78-point loss turned on this alone, and it is the second straight week it happened
Jameson Williams started during Detroit's bye for 0.0 — an avoidable roster-management zero, not a projection miss
Brian Thomas 0.0 at WR1 for the second straight week; the depth-3 listing in the context is now corroborated by production and he is no longer a default starter
Josh Jacobs 0.0 again from the bench (depth 4, bench role) — he is functionally dead roster weight, not a bye-gauntlet answer
recap.self_grade: C- — the individual projections (Likely, Harvey, Burden) were fine, but the packet again failed to prevent zeros at QB and WR, and the Jacobs RB1 recommendation was flatly wrong. Two straight one-score losses created entirely by inactive/bye starters.

waivers.reason: BURN PRIORITY #1 ON THIS. We have exactly zero startable quarterbacks in Week 7 — Herbert is on the Chargers bye and Lamar is a 50/50 ankle. A zero at QB has already cost us two one-score games this season; a third is the season. McKee is confirmed as Philadelphia's starter with Jalen Hurts sidelined (he is rostered on IR by eo33), which means we are claiming a full-time starting QB in a top-tier offense, not a bye-week body. Bigsby is the drop because he is an IR'd RB5 occupying a live bench spot (unless Sleeper offers an IR slot — see bench note — in which case drop Keaton Mitchell here and skip the second drop). On the priority cost: #1 priority is only worth hoarding if a league-winner appears, and nothing in this FA pool qualifies — Omar Cooper and Konata Mumpfield are depth-4 and depth-2 flyers, Tyrone Tracy is third on the Giants' chart. Guaranteeing a functioning starting lineup is worth more than holding a lottery ticket at 1-5. FALLBACKS if the claim somehow fails: Geno Smith (1373, depth-1 NYJ, Week 13 bye) or Cam Ward (12522, depth-1 TEN), both grabbable in free agency after waivers clear.

Do NOT spend priority on this — submit it as a claim only if the app forces it, otherwise take him in free agency the moment waivers clear. McLaughlin is the top trending kicker in the pool, depth-1 in a Tampa offense that generates volume, and his Week 10 bye is irrelevant because Dicker reclaims the slot in Week 8. Mitchell is dead weight: Chargers bye this week, RB2 behind Hampton, 0.4 points in his last appearance. trades.pitch: You're 3-3 with seven running backs and four receivers, and two of those four (Rashee Rice, Caleb Douglas) are Out. You physically cannot fill your WR slots right now while you're sitting two startable backs every Sunday. I'll send you A.J. Brown — a true alpha WR1 in New England who's already off IR and back on the field — plus Josh Jacobs for depth, and I'll take Chuba Hubbard back. If you'd rather keep Hubbard, I'll do the same deal for Jaylen Warren instead. You turn your worst starting slot into an every-week WR1 and still roster McCaffrey plus three other backs. I need bodies in a backfield that's about to hit byes; you need a receiver this week.
trades.why_it_helps_me: Converts two players I cannot start — Jacobs is a healthy scratch in all but name (0.0 in back-to-back weeks, depth 4 in Green Bay) and A.J. Brown is Questionable and behind three healthy receivers in my lineup — into a weekly RB2/FLEX. My bye gauntlet is real: Harvey is out Week 10 and I'm down to Allgeier alone at RB. Hubbard or Warren gives me a startable back through the Week 14-17 playoff window, which is the only window that matters.
trades.why_they_might_accept: They have a 7-RB, 4-WR roster with two receivers ruled out — the positional math makes this nearly free for them. They give up the fifth-best back on their own roster and get the best receiver in the deal by a distance. Name value on Jacobs sweetens it; they can find out about his snap share on their own time.

get: or Alvin Kamara plus Keon Coleman

I'll send Jameson Williams, who just went for 18.7 and is Detroit's starting field-stretcher, plus Isaiah Likely, who has posted 23.9 and 32.4 in his last two as the Giants' every-down TE1. Back comes Jahmyr Gibbs. If Gibbs is untouchable, I'll do Williams and Likely for Alvin Kamara plus Keon Coleman instead. You already have Brock Bowers, so Likely is pure trade capital or injury insurance for you at the one position where you have zero depth — and you fix your receiver room without touching your top four backs.

Oronde Gadsden (depth-1 TE in Los Angeles) backs into the TE slot, and Jefferson, Burden and Brian Thomas still cover the receiver spots. At 1-5 I need one dominant asset more than I need three good ones — Gibbs is a weekly 20-point swing in the Weeks 14-17 window.
trades.why_they_might_accept: Eight backs, four receivers, one of them ruled out — they are leaving points on their bench every week. A one-TE roster taking back the hottest TE in the league plus a starting WR is a genuine roster-shape fix for a 3-3 team that wants to climb into the top four.

trades.pitch: You're 3-3 and rolling out Kirk Cousins as your only quarterback — that's the single biggest weekly points gap on your roster and you have no backup if he goes down. I'll send you Justin Herbert, a top-five fantasy QB with no bye left on his schedule, plus Tyler Allgeier as backfield cover with Jeremiyah Love out and Will Shipley on IR. I'd like Omarion Hampton back. You upgrade your starting QB by double digits a week, you replace the back you'd be moving, and you keep Garrett Wilson, Jaxon Smith-Njigba and your whole receiving core untouched.
trades.why_it_helps_me: Hampton is a lead back with three-down usage and his Week 7 bye is already behind him after this week — he's a plug-and-play RB1 for the entire playoff run. CONDITION: do not send this until Lamar Jackson is confirmed active and practicing in full, because Herbert is our only functioning QB until then. Reporting has Lamar targeting Week 7-8, so this becomes live in the next seven to ten days. Note this is mutually exclusive with the mrkw deal on the Allgeier side — if mrkw lands Hubbard first, substitute Josh Jacobs for Allgeier here.
trades.why_they_might_accept: They roster exactly one quarterback, and it's Kirk Cousins. A 3-3 team two games out of first does not win a title starting him, and they have receiver surplus but no QB insurance. Herbert is the cleanest positional upgrade available to them in this league.

confidence_notes: Highest confidence: the QB claim (we have no startable quarterback otherwise, and McKee is a confirmed starter with Hurts on IR), the kicker stream, and Jefferson/Burden/Likely in the lineup. Biggest risk, in order: (1) LAMAR — reporting puts him near 50/50 for Week 7, so the QB slot is genuinely unresolved until Friday's practice report and Sunday's inactives; the packet lists him as the roster-legal placeholder because Herbert is on bye and league rules forbid putting a non-rostered player in the lineup, but the operational instruction is to install McKee the moment the claim processes unless Lamar is cleared and practicing fully. Do not repeat the Weeks 5-6 mistake. (2) JOSH JACOBS — live injury reports say he's completely healthy, but the league context says depth 4 / bench role and he has back-to-back zeros. I have weighted the context and the box scores over the injury report here because this is a usage problem that injury reporting will never flag; if a Week 7 snap report contradicts that, he goes straight back to RB1 over Allgeier. (3) ALLGEIER vs HARVEY ordering is cosmetic — both start, the slot labels do not affect scoring. (4) A.J. BROWN's designation could flip him into the FLEX over Jameson Williams if he's cleared to a full workload. PROCESS CAVEAT: my live-search budget was exhausted after verifying Lamar's ankle, McKee's starting status, Jacobs' injury report and A.J. Brown's Questionable tag — I was NOT able to verify Week 7 individual matchups, the Cleveland DEF matchup, or kicker game environments, so the DEF hold and the specific choice of Chase McLaughlin over Jake Bates are the least-researched calls in the packet; both are low-leverage. News that changes this packet: Lamar cleared (start him, bench McKee, send the chacetheace48 trade), Lamar ruled out early in the week (McKee is mandatory — confirm the claim landed before Sunday), Hurts activated (McKee's value collapses, keep Geno Smith as the backup plan), or Sleeper offering an IR slot for Tank Bigsby (park him there and keep Keaton Mitchell one more week).
